strengths: Significant dataset contribution addressing real gap: MMEarth-Bench provides 5 global tasks with 12 aligned modalities and explicit geographic test splits, filling a clear need in EO benchmarking that existing work lacks

Comprehensive and honest benchmarking: Evaluates 7 diverse models across multiple seeds with transparent reporting, demonstrating that geographic generalization remains hard (4/5 tasks show substantial performance drops)
Practical model-agnostic method: TTT-MMR consistently improves performance across all models and task types without modifying model architecture, with <1 sec/sample inference cost
Strong scientific practices: Complete reproducibility information, extensive supplementary material with raw results, ablations, and visualizations enabling verification and future work
Clear presentation and commitment to open science: Well-written paper with effective figures, interactive visualization tool, and commitment to release data and code
weaknesses: Limited method novelty: TTT-MMR is a straightforward application of existing joint training and test-time adaptation concepts; per-modality gradient normalization is the only novel technical component and is incremental

Modest and inconsistent improvements: Performance gains from TTT-MMR are often small in absolute terms (Fig. 7), with improvements highly variable across tasks and sometimes starting from negative baselines (soil OC geographic)

Missing comparisons with other TTA methods: No comparison with TENT or other test-time adaptation baselines, making it unclear whether improvements come from test-time training generally or specifically from multimodal aspects

Incomplete analysis of method behavior: Limited ablations (no study of individual modality contribution or gradient normalization impact), unexplained cases where geographic batching underperforms random batching (Table 5), and lack of investigation into what useful adaptation signals emerge during TTT

Unexplored paradox about multimodal inputs: Figure 6 shows multimodal input sometimes hurts geographic generalization, contradicting the paper's motivation, but this critical finding lacks investigation or validation

Fundamental problem not solved: Paper identifies that geographic generalization remains hard for all models but doesn't solve it; TTT-MMR provides partial mitigation rather than addressing underlying causes
Linear probing shows different patterns from finetuning (Fig. S.13) suggesting fine-tuning regime issues, but this is not discussed or investigated
Dataset limited by single-timestamp design (no temporal dynamics), related task types (all environmental monitoring), and lack of analysis regarding spatial representativeness or collection biases

strengths: Well-designed multimodal benchmark addressing real gaps: 12 aligned modalities, global distribution, random + geographic test splits, multiple training regimes (5%, 50%, 100%)
Large-scale dataset: ~77K tiles across 5 novel environmental tasks with careful curation from authoritative sources (GEDI, WoSIS, IUCN)

Comprehensive benchmarking of 8 diverse pretrained models revealing important insights: geographic generalization remains poor, pretraining benefits diminish with sufficient data, randomly initialized multimodal models are competitive
Strong experimental rigor: three random seeds, detailed hyperparameters, extensive raw results, clear reproducibility plan
TTT-MMR is model-agnostic, works with any architecture/loss, demonstrates practical improvements especially on long-tail distributions with geographic batching
Geographic test split thoughtfully targets underrepresented regions (Africa) in labeled EO data, addressing real societal bias
Interactive visualization tool and commitment to code/data release enhance community value
weaknesses: Geographic generalization testing limited to single continent (Africa only)—claims of 'global' evaluation undermined by lack of multiple held-out regions
TTT-MMR method lacks novelty: straightforward application of existing TTA to multimodal setting without comparison to other TTA baselines (TENT, etc.); improvements modest (~0.01-0.03 R²)
Insufficient mechanistic analysis of why geographic generalization fails despite global pretraining—no investigation of representation shifts, error distributions, or specific domain shift sources
Critical information scattered across appendix: linear probing results, modality importance analysis, architectural details—weakens main narrative
Dataset design limitations: all tasks continuous (no diverse classification), single timestamp (no temporal dynamics), fixed 10m resolution, no discussion of label noise for remotely sensed proxies

Missing ablations: no systematic evaluation of different fusion strategies for multimodal models, no analysis of modality dropout during finetuning, limited modality importance analysis (one model/seed)

Method evaluation gaps: no comparison to simpler domain adaptation baselines, no convergence analysis for TTT iterations, statistical testing insufficient (overlapping error bars, limited significance tests)
Experimental design choices underexplored: parameter-efficient fine-tuning (adapters, LoRA) not compared, finetuning vs. linear probing insights relegated to appendix
